page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-240GB-1xH100 is a GPU-accelerated server virtualized via KVM on the x86_64 architecture. It features 12 physical cores from an Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processor running at 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 240.0 GB of system memory, providing 20.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is driven by a single NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPU with 80 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark results show top-tier performance in specific workloads. The server achieves an LLM inference speed of 10515.12 tokens per second for prompt processing and 547.27 tokens per second for text generation using a small 135M model, both placing in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression also reaches the top 10% tier at 15.51 GB/sec, while single-threaded gzip compression registers in the top 25% at 35.51 GB/sec. Other metrics, including a PassMark CPU score of 32078.76 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 26217.73, fall within the average range.

The high ratio of memory to vCPUs combined with the Hopper architecture GPU makes this server suitable for memory-intensive machine learning, large language model inference, and data science workloads. However, the shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage represent key architectural tradeoffs that require external storage solutions. The hardware profile offers high resource density for GPU-bound tasks, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that prioritize GPU memory and VRAM over dedicated, non-shared CPU cores.
